# Midterm Project {.unnumbered}

Week 7 has no new chapters. Instead, you put the first six modules to work on a single open-ended analysis: you are a data scientist for **Regork**, a national grocery chain, and your manager has asked you to identify a growth opportunity the company could invest in.

Everything the course has covered so far feeds into this. You will import and clean data, join tables, aggregate, visualize, and — most importantly — build a narrative that a business executive can act on. The analysis itself is only half the work; communicating it clearly is the other half.

## What You'll Do {.unnumbered}

- **Define a business question.** Growth opportunities can come from customer segments, seasonal trends, product relationships, or promotions. Your question may evolve as you explore, but the final report must state one main question and answer it fully.
- **Design an analytic approach.** Join at least two tables from the `completejourney_py` package and prepare them deliberately.
- **Dig past the first answer.** A strong project examines the question from several angles rather than stopping at the first chart that looks interesting.
- **Recommend something specific.** Tell the CEO what to do next, not just what the data says.

You will work in teams of 2–4, self-selected from the groups listed in Canvas.

## Deliverables {.unnumbered}

| Deliverable | Format | Notes |
|-------------|--------|-------|
| Written report | HTML exported from a Jupyter notebook | Named `YYYY_BANA4080_groupXX_finalproject.html` |
| Executive presentation | 3 minutes maximum | No code — visuals and business language only |

Grading totals 75 points, split between report components (40) and presentation components (35). The full rubric is on Canvas; read it before you start, since formatting and presentation each carry 15 points that are easy to earn and easy to lose.

## Getting Ready {.unnumbered}

You drafted project proposals in the Week 5 lab and submitted one for homework that week, so you should already have a question in hand. [Chapter 15](15-exploratory-data-analysis.qmd) is the closest model for what a complete analysis looks like — question, structure, distributions, segmentation, story. Work through that chapter's framework again with your own question before you start writing.
